basis: Skeletal dysplasia, diabetes and deafness define disease; dentin disease 4/4. Intellectual disability 4/4 omitted by cap; asthma and diabetic retinopathy are separate diseases.
Microcephaly and severe limb malformations define syndrome; pulmonary hypoplasia is a major feature of the lethal presentation, although its frequency is unquantified.
Interval-dependent duplication umbrella; neurodevelopmental impairment supports this provisional axis. Imprinting-region subtypes vary; no additional common organ damage established.
Nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing impairment in 8/8; macrocephaly in 1/8 does not establish neurologic disease.
Intellectual disability, strabismus and oral/maxillary abnormalities define syndrome; open bite and dental crowding 6/7. Hypermobility alone does not establish joint damage.
Tuberculous infection commonly occupies kidneys and urinary tract; genital involvement has no separate reproductive axis.
Encephalopathy and hearing loss define disease; scoliosis 3/3 and optic atrophy 1/3 (~33%). Neurogenic bladder 1/3 omitted by cap; cerebral visual impairment is neurologic.
Autoimmune inflammatory skeletal myopathy; interstitial pulmonary abnormalities occur in 30-79%. Cardiac disease is occasional (5-29%).
Developmental impairment and epilepsy define encephalopathy; visual impairment in 1/2 lacks evidence of intrinsic ocular damage.
Air-filled congenital lesion of the laryngeal wall; larynx belongs to the pulmonary axis.
Autoimmune blistering skin disease; stomatitis and oral mucosal blisters occur in 30-79%, establishing direct oral involvement.
Peroxisomal metabolic defect; neuropathy/seizures and pigmentary retinopathy reported in 1/2, with rod-cone dystrophy also documented. Infantile liver disease is rare.
Partial 8q duplication syndromes commonly cause developmental impairment; other malformations vary with the duplicated interval and lack a shared frequency threshold.
Dermal elastin loss; tibial abnormalities and lumbar hyperlordosis occur in 30-79%. High palate and irregular dentition alone do not establish oral functional damage.
Inherited parathyroid overactivity; bone loss commonly affects at least ~30% in sustained primary forms. Transient neonatal disease differs; renal stones are separate disease.
Definition specifies no intrinsic phenotype; disease from unmasked recessive mutations is separate. Phenotype annotations do not establish direct organ disease from UPD itself.
CRYBB2-related cataract directly affects the lens; cataract is obligate.
Folate-metabolism defect with epilepsy and CNS hypomyelination. Cerebral visual impairment is neurologic; short stature and short bones alone do not establish skeletal dysfunction.
Anterior chamber angle closure causes elevated intraocular pressure, optic nerve damage and visual field loss.
Intellectual disability and epilepsy accompany defining hypogonadism and diabetes; muscle atrophy is occasional and facial dysmorphism does not establish another damaged organ.
Urogenital sinus and perineal urethral malformations occur in 80-99%; urethra maps to renal. Gonadal differentiation alone does not establish endocrine dysfunction.
Persistent cognitive complaints define a cognitive disorder; objective neural injury is not required for this primary axis. No additional organ involvement established.
Skeletal myopathy and cleft palate define syndrome; ptosis occurs in 80-99%. Respiratory insufficiency reflects muscle weakness without established intrinsic pulmonary injury.
Spinocerebellar dysfunction and peripheral neuropathy define disease; muscle atrophy is neurogenic, without evidence of a separate direct myopathy.
Occupational airway disease; most cases involve sensitizer-induced immune-mediated asthma. Irritant-induced nonimmune cases are a minority; no other organ damage is intrinsic.
